scope: loopback ring bridge to a real IW4OL server; G2 still not accepted

static_findings.method: PE VA map + Capstone disassembly of the exact offline image (tools/disasm_image_1649370.py), plus a byte scan for absolute references

ring_a_outgoing.writer: 0x6750A0 branch arg1<1 (called from 0x6751F0 when the connection index is 0 and adr type == 2)

ring_b_incoming.consumer: 0x675140, only called from 0x4F8D70 (client receive pump); the shipped image never writes ring B

ring_c_server_slots.note: written when 0x6750A0 receives a connection index >= 1; unused by the local type-2 client slot

connect_entry.behavior: clears state, forces the address buffer to 'localhost' for the local branch, writes connection phase 7 then 4, parses 0xC7AF590 with 0x675390 into connection+0x14..+0x28, then calls the 0x5C05F0 phase machine

phase_machine.send_wrappers: 0x675260 and 0x675310 copy the text after a 0xFFFFFFFF marker and call 0x6751F0; 0x6751F0 forwards type 2 to 0x6750A0 and other types to 0x77FB80/0x622040

response_handlers.challengeResponse: 0x5C169F: 0x5C1300(phase 3), then connection+0x14.. receives the packet adr, +0x138 challenge, 0x5BE030(4) writes phase 4
response_handlers.connectResponse: 0x5C17C9: 0x5C1300(phase 4) compares the connection adr with the packet adr via 0x674D90; on success 0x674200 parses the info string, then 0x5BE030(5) writes phase 5

runtime_findings.session: codex-ring-bridge-2, private five-pack stage, natural Auth/LSG login to ui_state=5/auth_state=9/lsg_state=2
runtime_findings.server: 2697 codol_dedrun, mp_cross_fire, UDP 28970 (28969 could not bind while the client's WFP guard was active)
runtime_findings.bridge: tools/ring_bridge_1649370.py: reads ring A, writes ring B, calls 0x4F8D70 on the CODO window thread; the engine's own ring-A drain 0x674F30 was temporarily replaced by xor eax,eax;ret so packets survive, then restored
observed_sequence: client phase armed to 3; getchallenge 0 "0cf7ee44e08c4c28" (38 B) left through ring A and reached 2697 (server logged SV packet ... getchallenge)
the server's challengeResponse was written to ring B; the pump advanced the client to phase 4 (connection adr type 2 / port 0 / channel 0x9D)
the client then sent connect 0cf7ee44e08c4c28 "\name\...\xuid\...\challenge\1553576585..." (410 B); 2697 logged SV packet ... connect and CS_FREE -> CS_CONNECTED for AdministraClient num 0
a synthetic connectResponse injected alone advanced the live client from phase 4 to phase 5
after phase 5 the client produced 850-byte OOB stats packets: 0xFFFFFFFF 'stats' 0x00 index:u8 compressed:u16 + zlib stream; one stream inflates to exactly 32768 bytes

the profile header is not crc32(profile[4:]) for this build (observed 0x86AC2088 vs 0xB2BFEF12), so the 2697 archive handler rejects the upload; the bridge can rewrite only the 4-byte check word and re-compress
with the rewritten header 2697 received the stats packets, but the live run ended with 'Going to CS_ZOMBIE' and no 'stats complete' line; the client then timed out back to phase 0

conclusion: The client's own OOB connection protocol is now reachable without patching game code: getchallenge -> challengeResponse -> connect -> connectResponse -> phase 5 all executed through the engine's loopback rings, and the client produced a real 32768-byte stats upload. G2 is still not accepted because the map world was not loaded; the remaining gap is the stats/gamestate progression and possibly the packet injection order while netchan data is present.
